title: Justice Department Looks Into TV Networks Pausing Trump Pool Coverage
summary:
The U.S. Justice Department says it is investigating several major television networks over whether they broke competition laws when they briefly stopped sharing White House "pool" coverage of President Donald Trump.

In a press pool, a few reporters cover an event and share notes, photos, or video with many other newsrooms. Last month, five networks paused that shared presidential coverage for several days. They did so after the Trump administration took away credentials from reporters at CNN, MS Now, and Politico.

The Justice Department asked ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC, and Fox News for messages about the pool. Officials said a coordinated pause might violate the Sherman Act, a law meant to stop companies from joining together in ways that unfairly limit competition.

A department spokesperson said the Antitrust Division is investigating whether the news organizations violated antitrust laws. The networks have not yet commented, according to the report.

Earlier, Trump blocked those three outlets from White House access after accusing them of unfair coverage. A judge later ordered access restored after the outlets sued, saying the ban violated First Amendment press protections. The First Amendment limits the government from restricting press freedom based on the content of coverage.

The story also notes other recent fights over press access, including a February move to change who manages the White House press pool and a separate dispute involving the Associated Press. For kids learning civics, the core idea is that courts, newsrooms, and government agencies are arguing about how shared presidential coverage and competition rules should work.
why_it_matters: Shared White House coverage and competition rules shape what news many families can see. Understanding press pools and antitrust helps kids follow how democracy and media work together.

Competition, or antitrust, laws try to stop companies from working together in ways that unfairly limit rivals.
